modern: Death, like birth, is a mystery of nature: a putting together out of the same elements, and a taking apart into the same; and in no way a thing any man should be ashamed of, for it is not contrary to the nature of a reasonable being, nor contrary to the reason of our constitution.
original: Death is such as generation is, a mystery of nature; composition out of the same elements, and a decomposition into the same; and altogether not a thing of which any man should be ashamed, for it is not contrary to [the nature of] a reasonable animal, and not contrary to the reason of our constitution.
